title: Microtown 15min talk-track prep (engineer drop-in)
content:
Purpose: 15-minute microtown with engineering org lead drop-in (informal). Goal = 1) reassure on recent small-latency blips, 2) surface one clear ask for teams, 3) collect two quick success stories to highlight.

Format: 7 min update (me) + 5 min open q's + 3 min concrete next steps + quick feedback poll (emoji). Keep language plain.

Talking points (short bullets, read, don't lecture):
- Quick context: last week we saw 2 small latency regressions across eu-west clusters during high prefix load. Root cause traced to a kernel selection heuristic change rolled in canary (PR 412). No customer-facing errors; some routes saw +30ms p95.
- What we did: rolled back heuristic, enabled temporary throttling on affected routes, kicked off targeted rebench (tickets: ENGINF-893, ENGINF-898).
- Current state: steady; p95 trending back to baseline; dedicates/hosted unaffected for most customers. Monitoring alert thresholds adjusted to reduce noise.
- One clear ask to teams: if you see any unusual p95 from your route, post to #oncall-ops and attach a short sample (trace id + 3 example requests). That helps triage faster.

Q&A prep (anticipate):
Q: Will we change our rollout cadence because of this?
A: No broad cadence change. We will add an extra micro-canary (smaller traffic) for kernel-selection changes and a focused perf-check checklist before full rollout.

Q: Is customer data at risk?
A: No. This is perf-only. No error escalation.

Q: How long until permanent fix?
A: We have a patch candidate in PR 420; plan to canary tomorrow during low-traffic window. Tests: perf bench + KV-cache smoke + end-to-end shortcode.

Quick success story (call for 2):
- Ask: anyone who shipped a perf tweak that reduced p99 or cost — DM me one sentence and the metric change. We'll highlight 1-2.

Notes to self / prep checklist (do these before show):
- Confirm dashboard snapshot + 1x short p95 graph (last 72h) -> upload to slide 1. (Arjun)
- Paste links to PRs and JIRA in chat after talk. (Marta)
- Prepare fallback script if live question goes too deep: "we'll take the deep-dive offline with SRE & runtime team and follow up in Monday notes."
- Keep slide count to 1-2. No long bullets.

Unresolved / open items to follow-up post microtown:
- Decide exact micro-canary traffic fraction for kernel-selection patches (proposal: 0.5% -> 2% over 30 min). Action: engineering program to sign off. (Inez)
- Add a short perf checklist to release playbook (Confluence page).

Draft comms snippet for follow-up Slack post (copy-pasteable):
"Quick update from today's microtown: we identified and mitigated a small latency regression tied to a kernel-selection tweak rolled to canary. No customer-visible errors. Patch candidate and targeted canary scheduled for tomorrow. If you see any route regressions, please post an example to #oncall-ops with trace ids — helps us triage fast. Short doc + links: <Confluence link>"

Open TODOs in doc (short):
- small diagram showing rollback path (Arjun)
- confirm canary window with infra (Inez)
- collect 2 success story bullets by EOD Thu (All)

Slack trails / refs: #oncall-ops (3/9 thread), #runtime-kernel (PR discus), spike note: /docs/perf/spikes.

Tone notes: keep it calm, engineering-first, admit uncertainty where it exists, emphasize measurable next steps. Avoid jargon-heavy descriptions — audience will be cross-functional.
